summary:
ASTRIS 2.3 - Public AI is a web-based prototype designed to support astronaut health monitoring during long-duration space missions. The system provides a centralized platform for tracking key health indicators, including heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation, body temperature, and glucose levels.

The platform offers two user roles: Crew members, who can monitor their personal health data, and Ground operators, who can oversee the health status of all crew members. It combines statistical analysis, trend detection, forecasting algorithms, alerts, and AI-assisted health insights to help identify potential health deviations and support timely decision-making.

By integrating artificial intelligence with data visualization and predictive analytics, ASTRIS aims to demonstrate how intelligent software can support astronaut health management, improve situational awareness, and contribute to safer human space exploration.
details:
ASTRIS 2.3 - Public AI is an intelligent web-based prototype developed to demonstrate how artificial intelligence and data analytics can support astronaut health monitoring during space missions.

How the system works

The application provides two main user roles: Ground Operator and Crew Member. The Ground Operator has access to the health information of all six astronauts and can monitor their indicators, review alerts, and oversee changes in their condition. Each Crew Member has access to an individual dashboard displaying personal health indicators, historical data, charts, forecasts, notifications, and a health journal.

The system monitors five key health parameters: heart rate, systolic and diastolic blood pressure, blood oxygen saturation (SpO₂), body temperature, and glucose levels. It also supports recording sleep duration and subjective wellbeing through the journal.

Data analysis and artificial intelligence

ASTRIS combines statistical methods and AI-assisted analysis. It uses moving averages (SMA and EWMA), statistical deviation detection, trend analysis, and forecasting methods such as Holt's method and autoregressive models (AR(2)). These techniques help identify unusual changes and estimate possible future trends.

The AI component integrates GPT4Free and PollinationsAI to generate contextual analysis based on available health indicators, historical records, forecasts, alerts, and journal entries. The results are organized into observations, limitations, and suggested next steps. If the external AI service is unavailable, the application can provide a clearly identified statistical fallback analysis.

Technologies and implementation

The prototype was developed using HTML5, CSS3, and JavaScript for the user interface and client-side functionality. Node.js provides server-side logic, API endpoints, and authentication, while Python is used to support the AI component. Docker is used for application containerization, and Render was prepared as a deployment platform.

The application includes role-based access, password hashing, server-side session management, interactive dashboards, data visualization, alert management, and automated analysis.

Innovation and expected impact

The main innovative aspect of ASTRIS is the combination of health data visualization, statistical forecasting, alert management, and AI-assisted interpretation in one accessible platform. Instead of presenting isolated measurements, the system aims to help users understand changes over time and identify potentially important deviations.

ASTRIS is currently a prototype using simulated health data rather than measurements from real medical sensors. It is intended as a demonstration of the software architecture and analytical approach, not as a certified medical diagnostic or decision-making system.

In the future, the project could be extended through integration with real wearable sensors, persistent database storage, improved communication synchronization, specialized AI models, and validation using relevant biomedical research data. These improvements could help develop ASTRIS into a more comprehensive astronaut health monitoring support platform.
